reading.body:
Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 1 in Douglasville, Georgia, publishes 22.5 MW of IT capacity across 205,000 square feet of technical space, operated by Flexential.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 2250 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 562 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 1 holds 6 published certifications: SOC 2 Type 2 (audited controls over security, availability, and confidentiality, tested over time rather than at a point), PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), ITAR (a specific compliance or security standard), NIST 800-53 (alignment with the federal security control catalog), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Georgia has 7 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 66.3 MW. Flexential Atlanta - Douglasville 1 contributes 22.5 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
